questions.q: What is distinctive about a VARRAY?
options: It has a fixed maximum size set at declaration and can never grow past it
It can only be indexed by string, never by integer
It is unbounded and can be used as a database column type
It exists only inside packages, never in anonymous blocks
questions.explain: VARRAY (variable-size array) declares its maximum size up front — e.g. VARRAY(5) — and that ceiling never changes.

questions.q: What can a Nested Table do that a VARRAY cannot?
options: Grow with no fixed upper bound, and be used as a real database column type
Be indexed by a string key
Exist only in memory with no database equivalent
Hold a maximum of exactly 5 elements
questions.explain: Nested Tables are unbounded and, unlike VARRAYs, can be used as an actual column type in a database table.

questions.q: Which PL/SQL collection type is most similar in spirit to a dictionary or hash map?
options: Associative Array
VARRAY
Nested Table
SYS_REFCURSOR
questions.explain: An Associative Array can be indexed by a string key, exists only in memory, and is the collection type reached for most often in ordinary procedural code.

questions.q: What does INDEX BY VARCHAR2(30) specify in a collection type declaration?
options: That the collection is an associative array keyed by a string type
That the collection has a fixed maximum of 30 elements
That the collection can be stored as a database column
That the collection must be declared inside a package body
questions.explain: INDEX BY makes a TABLE OF type an associative array and specifies the key type used to look up elements.

questions.q: Why don't T-SQL table variables or temp tables closely match any PL/SQL collection type?
options: They are real database-engine row sets with their own storage and optimizer involvement, not in-memory PL/SQL-only constructs
T-SQL table variables are indexed by string keys just like associative arrays
T-SQL table variables have a fixed maximum size just like a VARRAY
T-SQL has no concept of a table variable at all
questions.explain: T-SQL table variables involve the real database engine; PL/SQL collections (except Nested Table columns) are purely in-memory, language-level constructs.
